clue.text: Gathered deceived guards very gullible in the end

indicators.note: whoever guards something stands around it, so one word wraps the others
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: conned means tricked or deceived
V is the standard abbreviation for very
the final letter of gullible

explanation.surface: A crowd assembles, having fooled someone extremely credulous.
explanation.walkthrough: CONNED holds V plus E, making CON-V-E-NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to meet or assemble, so convened is a synonym for gathered in the past tense.

clue.text: Dramatic work couples read regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken and the rest skipped

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Pairs of actors take turns reading a play aloud at a rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, an example of a dramatic work.

clue.text: Welshman aboard ship in Portsmouth saying farewell

indicators.note: someone aboard a vessel is inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: Aled is a Welsh man's name, as in the singer Aled Jones
HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship, is preserved at Portsmouth

explanation.surface: A Welsh sailor bids goodbye from the deck of a ship docked at the English naval port.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory is Nelson's flagship, kept in dry dock at Portsmouth, the English naval base.
explanation.definitionFit: Valedictory describes words or speeches given on parting, so it means bidding farewell.

clue.text: Bananas and nori unknown dietary option

indicators.note: to go bananas is to go crazy, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A menu listing bananas and seaweed as a mysterious diet choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas and nori look like the menu items, but bananas is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-dairy choice is one free of milk products, an option on a restricted diet; the adjective fits as a modifier.

clue.text: Rebuke island servant for casual affair

blocks.note: to dress down is to scold
Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's servant on his island

explanation.surface: Scolding a castaway's helper for being too relaxed about things.
explanation.walkthrough: Friday is the servant Crusoe finds on his island in Defoe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress-down Friday is a workplace custom of wearing informal clothes at the end of the week, hence a casual occasion.

clue.text: Happen to predict current date getting disheartened

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so only the outer letters survive

blocks.note: to bet that something will happen is to predict it
I is the symbol for electric current
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone forecasting their next romantic outing grows downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: DATE loses its middle letters to leave DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide is an old verb meaning to befall, as in 'woe betide you', so it means happen to.

clue.text: Give choice over whiskey

blocks.note: the choice item is the best one
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Offer a premium pick instead of a glass of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present or confer as a gift, a formal synonym for give.

clue.text: Raised arm to give name

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: gat is slang for a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: Putting a hand up to volunteer one's name in class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label or nickname, so as a noun it serves as a synonym for name.

clue.text: Bit of wisdom in a test prevails

indicators.note: only a piece of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from inside wisdom through to the end of test

explanation.surface: A smart remark in an exam wins the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from wis-DOM through IN and A to TES-t.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dominates holds sway or wins out, so it is a synonym for prevails.

clue.text: Fellows either side of trellis oddly overlooked bird

indicators.note: a word placed on both sides of another surrounds it
the odd-numbered letters are ignored, so only the even ones remain

blocks.note: fellows are men
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Men standing by a garden trellis fail to notice a bird perched on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small falcon, a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Piece of cake somebody vacantly fed to each duck, say

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, a word keeps only its outer letters
food fed to something goes inside it

blocks.note: EA is the usual abbreviation for each
the first and last letters of somebody
duck is an example of game, wild birds hunted for food

explanation.surface: Someone absent-mindedly hands out cake to every duck on the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck, say' tempts as the definition, but the 'say' marks duck as an example of game, the hunted birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something effortless, and easy game means a simple target or task.

clue.text: Some ignored by good-looking worker

indicators.note: words ignored are left out of the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
handsome means good-looking

explanation.surface: A few people take no notice of an attractive labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDSOME without SOME leaves HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand or deckhand, so it is a synonym for worker.

clue.text: Vanishing muscles: disadvantage eating away from home

indicators.note: something away from a place is taken out of it

blocks.note: abs are abdominal muscles
pros and cons: a con is a drawback
dining means eating
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A complaint that your six-pack fades when you keep eating in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: DINING loses IN to leave DING. 'Eating away from home' reads as dining out, but it is a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Absconding means running off secretly, so the person disappears; vanishing is a fair synonym in the participle form.

clue.text: Lacking enthusiasm in being upright?

blocks.note: first meaning: unwilling, reluctant
second meaning, read as a pun: not inclined, so not leaning at all

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: split as DIS-INCLINED it means un-tilted, which is standing straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant is not inclined to act, and something not inclined or tilted stands vertical.

clue.text: Piece of music playing, sure winner when in company

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a show that is on is being performed
a cert is a racing certainty

explanation.surface: A musical work that is a guaranteed hit when performed with others.
explanation.walkthrough: A cert is British racing slang for a horse certain to win, short for certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a composition for a solo instrument with orchestra, an example of a piece of music.

clue.text: Unlimited concerns with AI computer following partner

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, the first and last letters

blocks.note: bothers are worries or concerns
HAL 9000 is the artificial intelligence in 2001: A Space Odyssey
f. is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: Endless worries about an AI machine trailing one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTHERS loses its ends to give OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: One's other half is an idiom for a spouse or romantic partner.

clue.text: Hollow articulated apparatus

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a set is an apparatus, such as a television or radio set

explanation.surface: A piece of jointed but hollow equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' looks like it means jointed, as in an articulated lorry, but it means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is a badger's burrow, a hollow dug in the ground.

clue.text: Upcoming singer bathed in light is not bad

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
something bathed in a liquid is surrounded by it

blocks.note: a bass is a low male singer
pale means light in colour

explanation.surface: A rising vocalist lit by a spotlight gives a decent performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming singer' reads like a new star on the rise, but in a down entry it just turns the singer upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or acceptable, so it is a fair synonym for not bad.

clue.text: I'm disappointed by satellite's state

blocks.note: 'oh' is a sigh of disappointment
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: Someone let down by the condition of a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: New senate's amended order

indicators.note: something amended has been changed, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written, with the s

explanation.surface: A legislature reforms its standing orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a rule the senate amends, but it is the definition meaning tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness, the state of being in good order.

clue.text: Ruins of French port city bar to left

indicators.note: bar means except, so the following letters are excluded

blocks.note: de is French for of
Bristol is a port city in western England
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The wreckage of a French harbour town, with a bar on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: BRISTOL minus TO and L leaves BRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something destroyed, so it is a synonym for ruins as a plural noun.

clue.text: Old men having Sage Derby with last of their crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order
the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of their

explanation.surface: Elderly men eating a sage-flavoured cheese on their biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is an English cheese flavoured with sage, and crackers looks like the biscuits it is served with.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, from the grey beard of age.

clue.text: Want hems of baggy trousers to be cut

indicators.note: the hems are the edges of a garment, pointing at the first and last letters
cutting those edges off removes them from the word

blocks.note: slacks are loose casual trousers

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to have the bottoms of their loose trousers shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: SLACKS loses its first and last letters to leave LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and lack are both nouns for an absence or shortage of something.

clue.text: Uncorrupted tribe defending base

indicators.note: defenders form a ring around what they protect

blocks.note: a clan is a tribe or family group
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An honest tribe protects its home camp.
explanation.walkthrough: In maths, e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the sense of honest or free of corruption, as in a clean record.

clue.text: Dull colour was concerning

blocks.note: matte describes a dull, unshiny finish
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A drab paint shade caused some worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was concerning' reads as worrying, but here it means was of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that mattered was significant, and concerning in the sense of being relevant or important.

clue.text: Picked up Asian garment

indicators.note: picked up as in heard or caught by ear

blocks.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand

explanation.surface: Someone collected a piece of Asian clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is an item of clothing, so it counts as a garment.

clue.text: Messed up losing line and stopped

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken out

blocks.note: bungled means botched
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone botched things, dropped a line and gave up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunged as in bunged up means blocked or plugged, so it is a synonym for stopped.

clue.text: Course where tee is found?

blocks.note: tee is the letter T; its place in the alphabet is right behind S

explanation.surface: A golfer asking where on the course the tee is.
explanation.walkthrough: Tee is the letter T, which sits after S; afters is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is informal British for pudding, the course that comes after the main meal.

clue.text: Giving lie, dying to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deathbed confession: someone telling a falsehood while dying, hoping to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding means giving way or bending under pressure, so it matches giving as a participle.
